name: How do you know if a ground-up construction bid is too low?

mainEntity.name: What warning signs show that a bid for a Los Angeles custom home is unrealistically low?
mainEntity.text: What warning signs show that a bid for a Los Angeles custom home is unrealistically low?

acceptedAnswer.text: A suspiciously low bid usually means something important is missing. Common omissions include grading, utility upgrades, permits, engineering, site protection, landscaping, fixtures, or premium finish allowances. Another warning sign is vague language that does not clearly define what materials and labor are included. Low bids can also indicate that the contractor expects to add costs later through change orders. The safest way to evaluate a bid is to compare scope, exclusions, allowances, and assumptions rather than just the bottom line. For a custom home, a realistic proposal should explain how the project will be built, not just what the final number is. If one bid is far below the others, it deserves extra scrutiny before it is accepted.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bid is often too low if it leaves out site work, allowances, permits, engineering, or finish details that will still be needed later. Unrealistically low pricing can also signal weak scope definition or a contractor planning to recover costs through change orders. A complete bid should be detailed enough to compare line by line.
